description: Fair / industry-standard clause examples per the ClauseGuard 7-category taxonomy. Loaded into Chroma by Agent 2 (Comparator).

Payment: All fees are clearly itemised before purchase, and no additional charges are added without the customer's prior written consent.
The customer may cancel within 14 days and receive a full refund of any fees paid, with no cancellation penalty.
Late fees, if any, are limited to a reasonable amount and are disclosed in advance in writing.
Price increases require at least 30 days advance written notice and the customer may terminate before the increase takes effect.
The security deposit is held in a separate account and returned within 30 days of termination, less any itemised and documented deductions.
Billing errors must be corrected promptly, and the customer is given a reasonable opportunity to dispute any charge before collection.
No hidden or surprise fees may be charged; any ancillary cost must be clearly stated in the initial agreement.
The customer is entitled to a pro-rated refund for any unused portion of a prepaid service period.
Payment obligations are suspended while a good-faith dispute over the charge is being resolved.
Any interest or finance charge is capped and may not exceed the maximum rate permitted by applicable law.
The provider must notify the customer before automatically charging a payment method on file for recurring services.
Fees for optional add-ons require express opt-in and are never bundled into the base price without consent.
If the service is unavailable for more than 7 days, the customer receives a proportionate credit or refund.
The provider bears its own administrative costs and may not pass undisclosed processing fees to the customer.
Discounts and promotional pricing remain valid for the stated period, and expiry terms are disclosed up front.
The customer may pay by any lawful method and is not required to authorise unlimited future charges.
Termination fees are prohibited unless they reflect actual, reasonable costs incurred and are disclosed before signing.
Any prepayment is credited to the customer's account and refundable on a pro-rata basis upon early termination.
The provider must provide an itemised invoice for every recurring charge, and disputes are accepted within 60 days.
Price is locked for the initial term and may only change upon renewal with the customer's informed consent.
In the event of a billing dispute, the provider will not refer the account to collections until the dispute is resolved.
Any non-refundable fee must be expressly labelled and the customer must acknowledge it separately before purchase.
Auto-Renewal: Either party may terminate this agreement at any time with 30 days written notice, with no penalty or exit fee.
Automatic renewal requires the customer's affirmative consent and at least 30 days notice before renewal.
The customer may cancel through the same simple channel used to sign up, including online and by email.
Upon termination, the provider will promptly refund any prepaid fees for services not yet rendered.
The provider may terminate only for material breach after giving the customer a 15-day opportunity to cure.
Notice of non-renewal may be given up to the last day of the current term, and no long notice window is imposed.
If the provider materially changes the terms, the customer may terminate without penalty within 30 days of notice.
Termination for convenience is available to the customer with 30 days notice and without a termination fee.
The agreement does not automatically renew and expires at the end of the stated term unless both parties agree to extend.
The customer's cancellation is effective immediately upon request for month-to-month services.
The provider must send a prominent renewal reminder at least 30 days before any automatic renewal.
Upon termination, the provider returns or securely destroys customer data within 30 days at the customer's direction.
Death, disability, or relocation beyond the service area entitles the customer to cancel without penalty.
The provider may not continue charging after a valid cancellation request has been received.
Any trial period converts to a paid plan only with the customer's explicit confirmation.
The customer may downgrade or change plans at any time without penalty, with changes effective the next billing cycle.
Suspension of service for non-payment requires prior written notice and a reasonable grace period.
If the provider discontinues the service, it will provide at least 60 days notice and a pro-rata refund.
Termination rights are mutual and may not be exercised by the provider on less favourable terms than the customer.
Cancellation requests submitted online are deemed valid without requiring a phone call or written letter.
The customer is not liable for fees accruing after the effective date of a properly submitted cancellation.
A notice period longer than 30 days is not required for cancellation and must be proportionate to the billing cycle.
If the customer terminates for the provider's breach, all prepaid but unused fees are refunded in full.
Liability: Each party is liable only for its own negligence or wilful misconduct and liability is apportioned fairly.
Any cap on liability is limited to a reasonable multiple of fees paid and does not apply to gross negligence or fraud.
The customer is not required to indemnify the provider for claims arising from the provider's own acts or omissions.
The provider indemnifies the customer against third-party claims arising from the provider's breach or negligence.
Neither party excludes liability for death, personal injury, or fraud, which cannot be limited by law.
Damage caused by the provider's equipment or personnel is repaired or compensated by the provider.
The customer is liable only for damage caused by their own breach, and the provider bears ordinary wear and tear.
Consequential and indirect damages are mutually excluded, rather than waived only by the customer.
The provider maintains adequate insurance covering its operations and will provide proof on request.
Any waiver of liability must be reasonable, clearly highlighted, and not extend to the provider's own fault.
The customer's total liability is capped at the amount of fees paid in the preceding twelve months.
Claims must be brought within a reasonable limitation period and the provider may not unreasonably shorten it.
Third-party claims are defended by the party at fault, and the other party is notified promptly.
The provider is responsible for the acts of its subcontractors as if they were its own.
Liability for data breaches is not capped below the level required to make the customer whole.
The customer may withhold payment of disputed amounts without being deemed in breach.
Each party warrants it has authority to enter the agreement and will comply with applicable laws.
If one clause is found unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue in full force.
The provider does not disclaim responsibility for defects in the service it supplies.
Indemnification obligations are reciprocal and proportionate to each party's degree of fault.
The provider compensates the customer for losses caused by negligent service interruptions.
Any limitation of liability is conspicuously disclosed and cannot be buried in boilerplate.
Data Privacy: The provider collects only the personal data necessary to deliver the service and does not sell it to third parties.
Sensitive data such as biometrics, health, or financial information is collected only with the customer's explicit opt-in consent.
The customer may access, correct, export, and delete their personal data at any time.
Data is encrypted in transit and at rest using industry-standard protocols.
Personal data is shared with third parties only under written data-processing agreements and only as necessary for the service.
The provider will notify affected users and regulators of a data breach without undue delay and within 72 hours.
Data is retained only as long as necessary and then securely deleted or anonymised.
The provider does not use customer data for advertising or profiling without separate, revocable consent.
Customers may opt out of non-essential data collection without losing access to the core service.
The privacy policy is written in plain language and material changes require 30 days notice.
Access to personal data is restricted to authorised personnel bound by confidentiality obligations.
The provider complies with applicable privacy laws including GDPR, CCPA, and similar regimes.
Cookies and tracking technologies are used only with consent and can be disabled by the user.
The provider will not transfer personal data to jurisdictions lacking adequate protection without safeguards.
Upon account closure, all personal data is deleted within 30 days except where retention is legally required.
The customer may withdraw consent to data processing at any time, and withdrawal is as easy as giving consent.
Third-party service providers are vetted for security and are prohibited from using data for their own purposes.
The provider maintains an auditable record of data-processing activities and security incidents.
Biometric data, if collected, is stored as a non-reversible template and never shared commercially.
Minors' data is not collected without verifiable parental consent where required by law.
The provider will provide a copy of all data held about the customer upon written request, free of charge.
Data-security practices are independently reviewed and the provider maintains appropriate certifications.
Dispute: Disputes are first addressed through good-faith negotiation before any formal proceedings.
The customer may bring a claim in a court located in the customer's own jurisdiction of residence.
Any arbitration is optional and does not prevent the customer from seeking relief in small-claims court.
Class-action waivers are not imposed, preserving the customer's statutory rights.
Governing law is that of the customer's place of residence or a neutral, reasonably connected jurisdiction.
Mediation costs are shared equally and each party bears its own legal fees unless otherwise awarded.
Notices of dispute are delivered in writing with details of the claim and a 30-day resolution window.
The parties agree to continue performing their obligations while a dispute is being resolved.
The customer retains the right to seek injunctive or equitable relief in court where appropriate.
Any forum-selection clause must be reasonable and not impose an undue burden on the consumer.
The provider will reimburse reasonable arbitration filing fees that exceed the cost of court filing.
Arbitration, if used, is conducted by a neutral provider with a readily accessible consumer process.
English-language proceedings and translations are provided so the customer can understand the process.
The customer's local mandatory consumer-protection rights are not overridden by the agreement.
Decisions are reasoned and appealable to the extent permitted by applicable law.
Neither party is required to litigate in a distant, inconvenient forum.
Confidentiality of settlement discussions is mutual and does not restrict disclosure required by law.
The provider may not unilaterally select an arbitrator affiliated with the provider.
Small-value disputes may be resolved through an accessible online dispute-resolution platform.
Claims may be brought on a consolidated basis where they arise from the same conduct, at the customer's option.
The governing-law clause does not deprive the customer of the protection of mandatory local laws.
Any amendment to dispute-resolution terms requires clear notice and prospective-only application.
Warranty: The product is covered by a 24-month limited warranty against defects in materials and workmanship.
The warranty covers the cost of replacement parts and repair labour for the entire warranty period.
Warranty claims may be filed online or by phone and are resolved within 7 business days.
The consumer may register the product for warranty within 30 days of purchase at no charge.
Standard wear and tear is excluded from warranty coverage and is clearly explained to the buyer.
The warranty covers this product only and does not cover damage caused by misuse or unauthorised modification.
If a warranted defect cannot be repaired, the consumer receives a replacement or a full refund.
Warranty help is available in the consumer's local language and time zone.
Receipts are not required for warranty service if the product is registered with the manufacturer.
Third-party accessories do not void the warranty of the main product.
The consumer may choose repair, replacement, or refund for a defect reported within the first 30 days.
Warranty service includes free return shipping when the product must be sent for repair.
The warranty transfers with the product if the consumer resells or gifts it.
The manufacturer publishes the warranty terms on its website in plain language.
Claims for the warranty are accepted at the store where the product was purchased.
The warranty does not require the consumer to purchase extended coverage as a condition of the base warranty.
Software updates that fix defective functionality are provided at no cost during the warranty term.
The consumer is notified in writing if a warranty term changes, and the change applies only to future purchases.
The warranty explicitly lists the exclusive remedies available if a defect is found.
Any statutory consumer rights are in addition to, and not limited by, this warranty.
The warranty period restarts for replaced parts and repaired products.
Batteries and consumable parts are covered for a clearly stated shorter period that is disclosed up front.
The manufacturer may not void warranty claims for using recommended alternatives to proprietary parts.
Warranty claims do not require the consumer to send mandatory and costly diagnostic fees.
The written warranty includes a plain-English summary, with the full details available on request.
Repair turnaround time is guaranteed within 15 days or the consumer receives a replacement.
The manufacturer covers defects caused by its own assembly errors even after the warranty ends for parts.
Extended warranty offers are optional and clearly priced before checkout.
The warranty covers latent manufacturing defects discovered after the term for a reasonable period.
Documents confirming warranty coverage are provided electronically and on paper on request.
The consumer can download the warranty certificate and claim form at any time.
Other: The customer retains ownership of all content, data, and materials they create or upload.
The provider receives only a limited licence to use customer content solely to deliver the service.
The provider assigns or licenses back to the customer all work product created specifically for the customer.
The provider's licence to customer content terminates when the agreement ends, and content is deleted on request.
The customer is not required to grant a perpetual or irrevocable licence over their intellectual property.
The provider indemnifies the customer against intellectual-property infringement claims relating to the service.
Feedback may be used by the provider without obligation, but the customer's underlying IP is unaffected.
Open-source components are used in compliance with their licences and do not restrict the customer's rights.
The customer's trademarks and branding remain the customer's property and are not used without permission.
Any joint inventions are governed by a separate written agreement addressing ownership and royalties.
The provider may use anonymised, aggregated data for improvement only where permitted by law.
The customer may export their content in a standard format at any time and for no additional fee.
The provider does not acquire ownership of customer content by virtue of hosting it.
Moral rights of the customer's creators are respected and not waived without consent.
The provider gives notice before using customer content in marketing and obtains consent where required.
The customer has the right to remove content, after which the provider ceases all use except legal retention.
The provider's pre-existing IP is licensed to the customer for use with the service under reasonable terms.
The customer is not required to assign copyright in custom deliverables that they commissioned and paid for.
Third-party content is used under valid licences and the provider passes through applicable usage rights.
The provider will not register trademarks or domains confusingly similar to the customer's marks.
Licences granted are non-exclusive, non-transferable, and limited to the purpose of the agreement.
The customer's confidential information and trade secrets remain protected and are not disclosed to competitors.
The provider commits to a defined service level with a minimum uptime of 99.9% and reports performance monthly.
If the service falls below the agreed service level, the customer receives automatic service credits or a refund.
Planned maintenance is scheduled in advance, announced to customers, and performed during low-usage windows.
Support is available during clearly stated hours with defined response and resolution targets.
The provider gives at least 12 months notice before discontinuing a product or materially degrading a feature.
Performance metrics are measured transparently and made available to the customer on request.
The provider will not materially reduce service functionality during the term without the customer's consent.
Critical incidents are communicated promptly with status updates until resolution.
The customer is entitled to a remedy if the provider repeatedly fails to meet agreed performance targets.
Service descriptions accurately reflect the features provided, and marketing claims are honoured.
The provider maintains a documented business-continuity and disaster-recovery plan.
Downtime caused by the provider's systems counts against the service-level calculation.
The provider offers a clearly defined escalation path for unresolved technical issues.
Updates and upgrades are applied without unexpected loss of data or functionality.
The customer is notified of any change that affects compatibility or requires action on their part.
Data backups are performed regularly and restoration is tested and available on request.
The provider responds to critical security vulnerabilities within a reasonable, stated timeframe.
The customer may monitor their own usage and is not subject to arbitrary usage throttling.
Training and onboarding are provided so the customer can use the service effectively.
The provider maintains compatibility with supported platforms and gives notice before ending support.
Service credits are the customer's remedy for performance shortfalls and are paid without requiring litigation.
The provider does not engage in deceptive practices such as bait-and-switch pricing or hidden throttling.
The parties agree that the entire agreement is contained in this document and any amendments require written consent.
The headings in this agreement are for convenience only and do not affect its meaning.
Either party may assign this agreement only with the other party's written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
This agreement is binding on and inures to the benefit of the parties and their permitted successors and assigns.
The parties have had the opportunity to obtain independent legal advice before signing.
Amendments to this agreement take effect only when signed by both parties.
Any provision held invalid will be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable.
The parties agree to cooperate in good faith on any reasonable request for information under this agreement.
No waiver of a breach is a waiver of any later breach of the same or a different kind.
Neither party may rely on prior oral representations that contradict the written terms.
The customer is provided a copy of the signed agreement and may download it at any time.
